races.name: Here Come The Girls EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cousin Rachel
runners_data.note: Karl Ryan yard in fair nick (5/31 in 14 days) and the horse has only one run to its name (8th, 6f, Good), but it is a natural hold-up type mapped forward on the race shape due to the rear being full — its actual running position will likely be further back than the map implies, which tempers its chance in a race where the pace is steady.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in her only start so far, but this middle-distance bred filly has more than enough pedigree to suggest a longer trip will help; plenty needed to get into contention here and yet to get off the mark.

runners_data.name: Lady Caroline Lamb
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley rides for the Charlie Johnston yard (6/47 14-day), and with only a single placing (3rd, 7f, Standard) on the card the style and trip profile are genuinely unknown — lightly raced and stepping up to turf 7½f, she is an open question from start to finish.
runners_data.comment: Forced to switch at a crucial point on debut, finishing third beaten three lengths — the form from that outing reads encouragingly and she is expected to progress for a top yard, bred to be at her best over longer distances; yet to win but the opening run was sufficiently promising to make her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here, Fern Clyde steps up to 7½f from a career best of 6f and brings a recent Good-ground win to her favour; Tim Easterby sends her out with a 7/98 14-day mark, and she wears a hood (hg:h) — with no rival to press her she can set her own tempo, though the step up in distance on turf remains a live query.
runners_data.comment: Won a maiden at Pontefract last time by half a length, applying herself well throughout on a stiff track — a leading trainer sends her here under a penalty wearing first-time headgear. Effective over 6f on good ground, though the extra weight may expose the narrow margin of that debut success.

runners_data.name: Little Lady Karen
runners_data.note: Karl Burke's filly (9/47 in 14 days) placed third on her sole start over 6f on Good ground, so she handles the surface; a genuine hold-up type stepping up to 7½f, she will likely need the pace to stack up and Shelley James to find clear running in the straight to produce her best.
runners_data.comment: Showed some greenness under pressure on debut, finishing third beaten five and a half lengths — should come on for that initial experience and is effective over 6f on good ground; the connections' stable landed this race last year, though she remains yet to score.

runners_data.name: Rogue Passion
runners_data.note: David Tudhope takes the ride for Ed Bethell (4/25 14-day) on this hold-up filly who finished fourth on her only start over 7f on Soft ground; the switch to Good to Firm and the slight drop in trip should suit, but like the other closers she is dependent on Fern Clyde setting enough pace to reel in.

races.paceDynamic: Fern Clyde is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, she should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the gates on Good to Firm ground over 7½f at Beverley. The three hold-up types — Cousin Rachel, Little Lady Karen, and Rogue Passion — will be tracking from off the pace, while Lady Caroline Lamb's unknown style leaves her positioning uncertain but unlikely to disrupt Fern Clyde's rhythm. With a single pace-setter dictating a sustainable, even tempo, this race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile, as the lead horse can control fractions and those sitting midfield may lack the injection of pace needed to pick off a well-positioned leader. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can truly accommodate at the rear, and Cousin Rachel — a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to the midfield map position — is the runner most likely to find its natural position further back than shown.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fern Clyde Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fern Clyde leads at her own pace and the hold-up pack fail to close the gap in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Fern Clyde leads at her own pace and the hold-up pack fail to close the gap in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Fern Clyde sets a strong enough pace and the closers find their stride through the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: If Fern Clyde sets a strong enough pace and the closers find their stride through the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unlucky-in-Running Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong and Cousin Rachel or a hold-up rival finds a clear run after being temporarily checked.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong and Cousin Rachel or a hold-up rival finds a clear run after being temporarily checked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Caroline Lamb, whose style is unquantified, finds a prominent position and produces an unexposed performance.
scenarios.body: If Lady Caroline Lamb, whose style is unquantified, finds a prominent position and produces an unexposed performance.

watchPoints.text: Fern Clyde's uncontested lead is the pivotal factor — if she escapes into a comfortable rhythm unchallenged through the early stages, tracking horses may simply find her too far ahead to peg back on the run-in.

Lady Caroline Lamb's unknown running style (tagged U) means she could slot prominently and act as an inadvertent pace-pusher — if she goes forward early she could force Fern Clyde to run faster than ideal and bring the closers back into play.

Cousin Rachel, a true hold-up horse, will likely race further back than the map position suggests — punters taking it at face value as a midfield runner may be surprised to see it deeper in the field than expected.

The step up in trip for Fern Clyde from 6f to 7½f is worth monitoring — she has never raced beyond six furlongs and whether she sees out the extra distance on a flat, right-handed track will define the outcome.

Good to Firm confirmed for this race (noted in the going report as Good to Firm for the 2:15) — all horses are tagged going=OK, so no surface concerns, but the fast ground will suit a prominent, pacemaking style and make late challenges harder to land.

races.name: Beverley Racecourse Supporting Racing Staff Week Handicap

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with a glowing recent profile — winner over 7f on good just 12 days ago under Jason Hart, and placed four of her last five on similar ground; C Johnston's yard is firing at 6/47 over 14 days and this pace setup hands her the ideal closing assignment.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time beaten half a length off the same mark, inclined to race with the lid off but still ran to form — landed a handicap at Musselburgh in April off a 2lb lower rating and is effective at 6-7f on a sound surface; should go well again.

runners_data.name: This Farh
runners_data.note: D Loughnane sends this confirmed hold-up mare here 17 days after a win over 8f on good, and her sim-going record of 3W6P from 15 runs is the best strike-rate in the field; hood (headgear) noted, and Rowan Scott is a capable northern jockey who will have her settled at the back before delivering late.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time off the same mark here, running to form at 7f on a sound surface and is a horse that enjoys dominating from the front — now tries first-time blinkers and has landed a handicap here previously on the penultimate start; the mark looks stiff but the ability to set the pace makes this a live each-way player.

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front-runner, boasting a remarkable recent sequence of five wins from six including three consecutive victories over 8f on good and standard; races with blinkers and carries a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 suggesting he may not dominate as freely here, but his natural talent means he must still be respected even if his positional advantage is diluted.
runners_data.comment: Five wins from his last six starts, landing a handicap off this same mark last time back on turf — suited by 6-8f on a sound surface and crucially escapes any penalty here; the consistent form strongly suggests another bold display.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Consistent older horse with two wins from seven runs at 8f on good, wearing tongue-tie plus cheekpieces; his trainer S England is running at a solid 4/11 over 14 days and he has genuine claims to hold a prominent berth in behind the leader, though the step back to 7½f from his recent 8f runs is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Holding good form until a below-par effort on softer ground last time, when racing conditions did not suit — back on fast ground at a course where previously successful, with a top jockey aboard and dropping 1lb in the weights; there is a case to make here.

runners_data.name: Midsummer Storm
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced three-year-old for K R Burke — a yard operating at an excellent 12/52 over 14 days — returning after 45 days off with only three career starts, all at 7-8f on good or standard; the limited form makes the going style unknown but Burke's record with freshened horses is a live angle.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in novice company throughout, finishing fourth on her latest start when just running out of steam after stepping up in trip off a break — the opening handicap mark looks lenient and the pedigree suits around a mile; lightly raced with more to offer, though yet to win.

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: Genuine front-running type by inclination with two wins from 15 runs on similar going, but the field's pace configuration means she is unlikely to secure her favoured early berth and has been redistributed to midfield on the map; a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 underlines that racing out of her natural position is a meaningful disadvantage, and T D Easterby's 14-day record of 5/84 does not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap here in April off a 2lb lower mark but has been inconsistent since and has never prevailed off the current ceiling — fourth last time running to form, and a top trainer at the course provides some encouragement; hard to be confident at this rating all the same.

runners_data.name: Evocative Spark
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old prominent racer wearing a visor, trained by John Riches whose small yard is only 1/2 over 14 days; three recent wins at 6-7f on good give him solid course-type credentials, though the slight step up to 7½f and the modest trainer strike-rate are checks on enthusiasm.

races.paceDynamic: Roaring Ralph is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only seven runners over 7½f at Beverley on good-to-firm ground, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without serious harassment. Coolree and Evocative Spark are both genuine prominent types who will press for early position behind him, creating a structured but not frenetic pace that should suit those racing just off the speed. The field does hold more prominent-inclined runners than can all secure their natural position — Sunny Orange is a true front-runner by inclination but has been mapped to midfield precisely because Roaring Ralph and the other prominent types will crowd that lane; Sunny Orange is most likely to be shuffled back from her natural berth. The race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can track a genuine, metronomic pace and finish through it, with Tattie Bogle and This Farh — both proven closers on similar ground — ideally drawn to exploit a well-run race from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph controls proceedings at a fair but unexaggerated gallop, allowing hold-up horses to track, quicken and reel him in.
scenarios.body: If Roaring Ralph controls proceedings at a fair but unexaggerated gallop, allowing hold-up horses to track, quicken and reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dictate
scenarios.trigger: If Coolree or Evocative Spark press Roaring Ralph hard enough to lift the tempo and soften up the closers.
scenarios.body: If Coolree or Evocative Spark press Roaring Ralph hard enough to lift the tempo and soften up the closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph secures a soft lead and the pace proves slow enough that he is never truly threatened in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Roaring Ralph secures a soft lead and the pace proves slow enough that he is never truly threatened in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If positional jostling early disrupts the prominent contingent and creates an uneven pace that a fresh or lightly-raced horse exploits.
scenarios.body: If positional jostling early disrupts the prominent contingent and creates an uneven pace that a fresh or lightly-raced horse exploits.

watchPoints.text: Tattie Bogle and This Farh — if Roaring Ralph sets a genuine front-running pace unchallenged, these two confirmed hold-up closers with the best sim-going records in the field are the primary danger to each other from off the pace.

Sunny Orange — watch whether D Fentiman attempts to push her forward from the gate despite the redistribution; if she clears to a prominent position early, the race shape changes and Coolree and Evocative Spark face a more contested battle for the stands-side berths.

Roaring Ralph — his STYLE_FIT tag of 0.92 indicates he may not fully dominate despite his brilliant recent form; if Coolree or Evocative Spark press him hard into the straight, his ability to hold on is a key pace lever to watch.

Midsummer Storm — K R Burke's 12/52 14-day trainer stat is the best in the race and this unexposed three-year-old returning fresh after 45 days could outperform market expectations if the pace plays to a fresh pair of legs in the final furlong.

races.name: Big Racing Weekender Next 3 And 4 July Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Three No Trumps
runners_data.comment: Placed here last time out, finishing three lengths third in a maiden, and a switch to today's shorter distance should play to her strengths — consistent across her three starts and effective at 8f on this type of ground; has more to show but back from a short break.

runners_data.name: Alterity
runners_data.comment: Showed some inexperience on debut, finishing four and a quarter lengths third, but should take a step forward for that experience — a rangy filly whose yard has a strong recent record in this race; effective around a mile and the profile suggests there is more improvement to come, even if yet to score.

runners_data.name: Feliz Navidad
runners_data.comment: By a high-class middle-distance sire, this gelding is unraced and steps into the unknown on debut — bred to appreciate around a mile and a clear market move would be needed to justify serious interest.

runners_data.name: Pepsea
runners_data.comment: Showed a consistent level in her opening starts, including a runner-up effort, and simply ran out of stamina when tried over a longer trip last time — effective at a mile on good ground and the drop back in distance should suit; in form, though a touch more is needed to get off the mark.

runners_data.name: Cherringham
runners_data.comment: Raced keenly on debut at Lingfield but still held a prominent position for a long way over 10f before tiring — should be far better suited by this faster surface and a trainer in form adds to the appeal; well bred and holding strong claims, even if yet to win.

runners_data.name: Tamzan
runners_data.comment: Fourth beaten two and a quarter lengths in a handicap last time, running consistently without threatening — effective at 8f with a top course jockey engaged; has had several chances already without getting off the mark and a step forward is required here.

runners_data.name: Regal Desire
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on her only start, beaten three and a quarter lengths in a race where she shaped with real confidence — effective over a mile on the all-weather and bred to get a bit further; should improve further and is the one all others are measured against on the form book.

races.name: Beverley Annual Badgeholders Handicap

runners_data.name: Bruce Banner
runners_data.note: Best form on Good ground and ran competitive races at 12-14f; visor-free and fresh on just 5 days' rest, likely to be nudged forward by default given the absence of a true front-runner, which puts him closer to the action than his hold-up tag suggests|
runners_data.comment: Consistent of late with a placed effort five days ago, beaten five lengths in a handicap — stays well at 12-16f with the best form coming on the all-weather, though acts on good ground too; first-time visor applied and worth consideration, yet to win.

runners_data.name: Lednikov
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran whose sole turf win came over 14f on Soft, and his Good-ground record over shorter trips is modest (0W2P from 3 runs); blinkers fitted, returns on 10 days' rest, and Elle-May Croot's inexperience at this level is a factor — may find himself pushed to the fore but lacks the quality to dominate from there|
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap from recent starts but has been out of form in the last three outings, most recently below par when returning to turf — still 3lb above the last winning mark and now wears blinkers for the first time; effective at 12-14f on a sound surface and a revival is possible.

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: All recent form on Soft or Standard — the switch to Good to Firm is an open question for this four-year-old; his hold-up style is genuine but the redistribution means he is unlikely to get the strong pace he needs to deliver his finish, and a 21-day absence adds uncertainty|
runners_data.comment: On a mark 2lb lower than when last landing a race, this is the second run after a wind operation and should come on considerably for the experience — a genuine out-and-out stayer suited by 2m-plus, acts on this ground, and our rating puts the selection at the head of this field; first-time blinkers could help.

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with a win on Good ground over shorter trips but exposed at this distance; wears no headgear, and Tom Kiely-Marshall takes over — the hold-up style is authentic but his Good-to-Firm record is poor (1W from 8 runs) and he is being asked to race out of position in this shape|
runners_data.comment: Held up by the way things unfolded last time, beaten two lengths here off the same mark — a veteran who has dropped considerably in the weights over time and has a proven track record at this course; trainer in form and stays 12f on any going, the penultimate run hinted at a revival.

runners_data.name: Princess Vivi
runners_data.note: Consistent form at 8f on Good and Standard, but stepping up to 1m4f is a significant trip increase; her best placed run came over a mile on Good, and the extra four furlongs on fast ground looks a stamina stretch — headgear change to hood and 27 days since last run add variables|
runners_data.comment: Placed here last time beaten three lengths but appeared to find the test insufficiently demanding — wears first-time blinkers and has limited miles on the clock for this type of race; effective between 7f and 9f on the all-weather, and while without a win, there is some scope for improvement.

runners_data.name: Arch Legend
runners_data.note: Consistent in form figures but never a winner in 15 runs on comparable going; his best placed effort came over 14f on Good, which is at least distance-relevant — however, his inability to win from any running style in this going band makes him a limited each-way proposition regardless of how the race unfolds|
runners_data.comment: Went too fast too soon last time and faded badly down the field — trainer out of form and on a long losing run; suited by a sound surface but very hard to make a positive case given the current figures and pattern.

runners_data.name: Satyress
runners_data.note: Harry Bethell's yard is live (2/2 in 14 days) and Satyress has placed form on Good ground at up to 10f; the step to 1m4f is unproven, and while her hold-up style suits a sprint finish in theory, she too is displaced from her natural position and her finishing kick in a truly-run race remains untested at this trip|
runners_data.comment: Back from a break and kept on to finish four lengths third last time off a 1lb higher mark — effective at 10f on good ground and the longer trip today could prove beneficial; yet to win in recent starts and the mark still looks stiff.

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: Deeply exposed hold-up performer with form figures of 9-0009 suggesting she is currently out of form; the step up to 1m4f on Good to Firm is new territory, and William Pyle's booking from a cold trainer (0/6 in 14 days) offers no encouragement — hood worn but the overall picture is uninspiring|
runners_data.comment: Struggled to make any impact even with headgear last time here, beaten nine and a half lengths, and the form across recent starts has been consistently poor — effective at 8-10f on a sound surface; very difficult to argue any case and the pattern of results is discouraging.

races.paceDynamic: With all eight runners carrying a genuine hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m4f Beverley handicap on Good to Firm turf faces a structural vacuum at the head of affairs — the early gallop will be tentative, likely slow, as nobody is naturally drawn to make it. The race will almost certainly develop into a dawdle before a sprint-finish from the home turn, compressing the field and eliminating any meaningful pace advantage. On Good to Firm ground over this trip at Beverley, a track that already rewards tactical racers who can quicken in the straight, this shape almost exclusively benefits horses capable of producing a sharp turn of foot in a short, intense finish — any horse that needs a truly-run stamina test is disadvantaged here. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear; Bruce Banner and Lednikov, as the two runners whose redistribution flag was not triggered, are most likely to find themselves pushed forward into a prominent role by default, even though neither is a natural pace-setter.

scenarios.title: Slow burn, sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is negligible throughout and the field bunches into a cavalry charge from 2f out
scenarios.body: If the pace is negligible throughout and the field bunches into a cavalry charge from 2f out

scenarios.title: Forced leader dictates

scenarios.body: If Bruce Banner or Lednikov is pushed forward and sets a modest but consistent gallop that strings the field out

scenarios.title: Closers find a gap late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally more honest than expected and the winner comes from off the pace in the straight
scenarios.body: If the early pace is fractionally more honest than expected and the winner comes from off the pace in the straight

scenarios.title: Stamina test, sole survivor

scenarios.body: If an unexpectedly strong pace develops and only the most durable stayer sees it out over 1m4f on quicker ground

watchPoints.text: Bruce Banner and Lednikov risk being shuffled into a pace-making role they are ill-equipped to fill — if either goes forward and stops quickly, they could cause interference as the field concertinas in the straight
The all-hold-up field means the early furlongs may see dangerous jostling for position as riders attempt to avoid being trapped at the back — watch for crowding on the turn out of the back straight
Satyress's trainer H Bethell is operating at a rare but sharp 2/2 in the 14-day window — a booking indicator worth monitoring even if the filly's redistribution discount tempers outright confidence

Good to Firm ground reported across all Beverley races today; any horse whose recent form has come predominantly on softer surfaces (Jedhi Knight, Lednikov, Dandy's Angel) faces an unconfirmed going question that could materially affect their finishing effort

With eight runners and no front-runner, draw position and early jockey decisions in the first furlong will be disproportionately influential — watch the opening quarter-mile to identify which horse(s) are forced to lead against their nature

races.name: Humberside Airport Handicap

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: D O'Meara's 4yo has course-and-distance and recent good-ground form in its favour, won over this trip 15 days ago, and as the lone confirmed pace-setter here it will get an uncontested lead — though the [STYLE_FIT] tag at 0.93 signals it is technically operating slightly outside its optimal comfort zone, which is worth a mild discount if the pace becomes messy.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Doncaster three starts back off a 3lb lower mark — effective over 10-12f on a sound surface and drops 1lb from a well-beaten latest effort; the mark still looks testing and there is ground to make up on the race leader on ratings.

runners_data.name: Mao Shang Wong
runners_data.note: Stablemate of the favourite under Mark Winn, this 4yo won over 10f on good ground and has course form, making it the most likely hold-up beneficiary if the front end weakens; naturally held up and suited to this trip, though its Southwell and Wolverhampton runs on standard ground are of limited relevance here.
runners_data.comment: A course-and-distance winner who showed progressive form until a poor effort up in class last time — back at the same level here on the same official rating, effective over 8-10f on this ground and carries two wins in recent starts; a significant upturn in form is required but drops into a far weaker contest.

runners_data.name: Helmsley
runners_data.note: Ian Furtado's 4yo carries tongue-tie and has placed over 12f on soft going, but its best recent effort came in a different context — a natural hold-up horse that has been mapped to midfield solely because the back of the field is saturated with closers, and its sequence of 6th-place finishes offers limited confidence.
runners_data.comment: Back in form when going down by three-quarters of a length in a close finish last time, off a 1lb lower mark — benefited from being ridden up with the pace at a sharp track, stays well over 10f and acts on this surface; first-time tongue-tie applied and the recent return to form looks genuine enough.

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 7yo is the most consistent horse in the field on similar ground, placing five times in eight good-ground runs and showing 2nds over 10f recently; a genuine hold-up performer who will need a strong enough pace from Percy's Daydream to reel in, and at 5 days since last run may be sharp enough.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a head last time off this exact mark, putting up a sound performance at the distance and going — back in form and our ratings place this firmly at the head of the market; without a win in recent starts but consistently close, and conditions are right.

runners_data.name: Titian
runners_data.note: Miss Camacho's 8yo wears a hood and has struggled for form recently (figures of 0-0-6-6-0), a true hold-up type pushed forward on the map only because the field lacks midfield runners — its actual profile is firmly at the rear, and the consistent tail-end finishes on good ground give little reason to expect a change of fortune here.
runners_data.comment: Failed to land a blow last time out having missed the break, finishing down the field in poor form — now 4lb below last winning mark and first-time cheekpieces are applied; effective over 8-10f on this ground but without a win in recent starts and needs a significant step forward.

races.paceDynamic: Percy's Daydream is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, will dictate a controlled, unchallenged gallop from the front over this 1m2f trip on good to firm ground at Beverley. The remaining four runners — Mao Shang Wong, Helmsley, Qitaal, and Titian — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning Percy's Daydream will face zero pressure early and can set a comfortable, sustainable tempo entirely on its own terms. Helmsley and Titian are true hold-up horses who have been mapped to midfield purely because the rear of the field is congested with closers, not because they will naturally race prominently; in reality, all four chasers are likely to track from the back half of this small field. This race shape heavily favours Percy's Daydream and any hold-up horse with the finishing speed to reel in a front-runner who has had a soft lead — though a truly uncontested gallop at a fair clip on good to firm ground often allows the leader to control the fractions and simply stay on, making early position the decisive advantage today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Percy's Front-Running Control
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream dictates an uncontested, measured pace and sustains the gallop into the straight.
scenarios.body: If Percy's Daydream dictates an uncontested, measured pace and sustains the gallop into the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finisher Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream sets an overly generous pace that leaves the closers with a genuine target to aim at in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Percy's Daydream sets an overly generous pace that leaves the closers with a genuine target to aim at in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream sets an injudicious gallop and fades sharply, leaving the race wide open for anything tracking.
scenarios.body: If Percy's Daydream sets an injudicious gallop and fades sharply, leaving the race wide open for anything tracking.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed horses manages to race closer than expected and times a challenge from a stalking position off the pace-setter's shoulder.
scenarios.body: If one of the redistributed horses manages to race closer than expected and times a challenge from a stalking position off the pace-setter's shoulder.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Daydream — watch the early fractions closely; if D Tudhope kicks clear and the gap to the chasing pack exceeds three lengths by halfway, the race is likely over as a contest.
Mao Shang Wong — watch its position turning for home; if it has tracked within two lengths of the leader rounding the final bend, it becomes a serious danger to the front-runner.

Qitaal — Connor Beasley has ridden this horse recently and knows its needs; if it is produced with a well-timed run in the final furlong rather than a long run, it is the most likely closer to land a blow.

Helmsley and Titian — both are natural hold-up horses forced into a race with no genuine midfield, so watch whether either unexpectedly gets dragged into a closer position than normal, which could accidentally suit them if the pace is genuinely strong.

Going confirmation — the going report consistently states Good to Firm for this race; any softening towards Good would modestly assist Helmsley (who has a 2nd on Soft) and reduce Percy's Daydream's front-running advantage on quicker ground.

races.name: Racing TV Extra On racingtv.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Ice Show
runners_data.note: D Tudhope booked for the O'Meara yard who are striking at 8/52 over 14 days — that trainer-jockey combination is the strongest tactical angle in the race; steps up from 7f on softer ground with only one placing from three runs on similar going, so the trip and conditions are a test but the finishing speed has been present.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten when tried over a shorter trip last time, which was probably not to advantage — out of a middle-distance sire and may do better now facing a more suitable distance in handicap company; yet to win and the form provides little encouragement, though the trip switch offers a reason to watch.

runners_data.name: Sahm Naif
runners_data.note: James Horton's yard is quiet (0/9 T14) but Jason Hart is a sound booking; the step from 7f/8f up to 1m2f is the key unknown and the form shows a 4th over 10f on good ground which is quietly encouraging, though four runs without a win or place on soft/standard may mean the better ground here is important.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth on handicap debut beaten six and a half lengths, broadly meeting expectations on that first handicap start — middle-distance bred and a big colt still learning the ropes; attitude has been a question mark in the past but it is early days in this sphere and there could be improvement ahead.

runners_data.name: Wadacre Geisha
runners_data.note: Johnston yard (5/45 T14) with Connor Beasley, and the form base is over 10f on good ground including a 2nd — the natural ability to handle this trip on this surface is the best thing she brings; placed into midfield on the map because the field is entirely hold-up types, so she races in her natural position but the redistribution note means no tactical edge is gained.|
runners_data.comment: Performed to a sound level at this track last time, beaten two and a quarter lengths off a 1lb higher mark — consistent across her starts and back on the fast ground she handles well; effective at 10f here and the mark is very workable, making her a clear favourite on our figures.

runners_data.name: King Of Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Jedd O'Keeffe's runner has been off 47 days which is the longest break in the field and is a concern for fitness sharpness in a sprint finish; all four recent runs have come on soft or standard ground and this good to firm surface represents an untested switch, with the form showing an 11th on good last time — this horse needs things to go right.|
runners_data.comment: Down the field on the most recent outing, which likely served as a needed pipe-opener — trainer in form and bred for 8-10f; should improve significantly now handicapping at a suitable distance and represents solid each-way claims at a price.

runners_data.name: Turton
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish tag, which is a direct red flag in a race guaranteed to end in a flat-out sprint; John Tate's yard has 3/12 T14 but the finishing profile is the wrong one here — the horse has been beaten progressively harder over the final furlong in recent starts on softer ground.|
runners_data.comment: Out of his depth over a shorter trip last time and never able to land a blow — bred for around a mile and first-time blinkers are applied today; should find the longer distance here much more conducive and is on a winnable mark, though yet to score.

runners_data.name: Resdev Time
runners_data.note: M & D Easterby's consistent but winless runner has placed once in nine similar-going runs and run five consecutive 5ths over 8f on good/soft — the pattern is one of a horse who finds its level without threatening; the step to 1m2f is longer than anything in the form book and that unknown trip must be respected alongside the inability to win.|
runners_data.comment: Denied a clear run when staying on well last time, beaten five lengths — down in the weights on a going she acts on, effective at 7f but not yet proven over today's mile; there is a case on the handicap mark if getting a trouble-free passage.

runners_data.name: Royal Sizzler
runners_data.note: Wears a hood, carries a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag, and Mike Dods is 0/27 T14 — three compounding negatives in a race decided by a sharp sprint; the form reads 5th, 10th, 11th across different ground and distances with no evidence of a strong closing effort, making this the hardest horse to be positive about.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten down the field in a novice when green and likely in need of the run — dam was a Listed-placed winner over 7f and there is some pedigree to work with; trainer without a winner at the moment and yet to show consistent ability, making this a speculative pick.

runners_data.name: Eva The Deeva
runners_data.note: N Tinkler has 6/26 T14 and Faye McManoman takes the ride; the lowest weight in the field (125lbs) is a genuine physical advantage in a tight sprint finish — the 7th of 8f on good last time is the most relevant piece of form and shows she handles the surface, but she has never won and the trip is a step beyond her best.|
runners_data.comment: Missed the break on handicap debut and never featured, beaten six and a half lengths — bred for 7f and above but has given nothing concrete to go on across four recent starts; very hard to argue a case at the current mark.

races.paceDynamic: This is a flat 1m2f handicap at Beverley on good to firm ground with eight runners, every single one of whom carries a hold-up style — there is no confirmed front-runner or prominent racer in the field. The race will drift out of the gates with nobody wanting to lead, almost certainly producing a dawdle through the early and middle stages before the field bunches and a sprint finish develops in the straight. All eight runners are true hold-up types who want to come from off the pace, meaning the winner will be determined by who quickens most sharply from a compressed group in the final two furlongs. This race shape strongly favours the horse who can accelerate most cleanly from a sprint finish on good to firm ground — raw finishing speed and a jockey prepared to commit early enough will matter far more than tactical position. Six runners including Wadacre Geisha, Turton, King Of Yorkshire, Resdev Time, Royal Sizzler and Eva The Deeva are tagged REDISTRIBUTED because the field holds more genuine hold-up types than the pace map can separate at the rear; none of these horses will get a meaningfully different position to Ice Show or Sahm Naif, so the race reduces to who has the sharpest sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Ice Show — watch whether D Tudhope commits early and uses the sprint finish to maximum effect; if Tudhope gets a clean run from the pack this horse has the best jockey-trainer combination in the race and must be tracked throughout.

Royal Sizzler and Turton — both carry headgear and fades-in-finish warnings in a race guaranteed to end in a sprint; if either is prominent on the turn-in before stopping, they could cause traffic interference for horses arriving late.

King Of Yorkshire — 47 days off the track on an untested good to firm surface is a layoff-fitness concern in a race where sharpness at the finish is everything; watch the market to see if money comes for this horse or drifts.

Wadacre Geisha — despite the redistribution tag she is the only runner with a placed run over 10f on good ground in recent form; if the pace is truly slow and the trip becomes a stamina test rather than a speed test, she moves into genuine contention.|

Eva The Deeva — the lightest weight in the field at 125lbs could prove meaningful in a bunched sprint finish where every pound counts; worth tracking whether she gets a clean run from the pack or becomes trapped in traffic.|

races.name: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Bethell in good recent form (2nd on good over 6f three days ago), holding fitness well; operates on this going without concern and the lone pace role on this 5f track is a clear tactical asset, though the STYLE_FIT tag is a reminder this horse has not always dominated from the front.
runners_data.comment: Went close last time, runner-up beaten one and a quarter lengths here on the same mark — back at a familiar course on the going she handles, effective at 5-6f; consistent in a short career with a workable rating and should remain very competitive.

runners_data.name: Jack Rabbit Slims
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 5f on good ground and wears headgear (tp), giving Nicholls something to work with tactically; a genuine hold-up operator who needs a wall of pace ahead of him to peel off, which may materialise if Oasis Cover goes hard, but the compressed field makes threading through traffic the chief danger.
runners_data.comment: Overraced in first-time cheekpieces last time, beaten four lengths here at the same mark — at best, has shown significant ability at course and distance over 5-6f on any going; inconsistent but on his day is a big player and cannot be dismissed.

runners_data.name: Dabbling
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears' 3yo has been racing in mid-to-rear positions and form reads 5-7-6 in recent good-ground sprints — consistent but not threatening enough to suggest a step forward here without a shift in race conditions; 19 days off the track is the longest freshen-up in the field and Kiely-Marshall will need to produce a bold tactical ride.
runners_data.comment: Missed the break last time and had no chance from that point, beaten eight lengths — a trainer in form and effective at 5f on a sound surface; inconsistent but a clear run would transform the picture and there is ability in there somewhere.

runners_data.name: Brain Freeze
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' colt owns the strongest credentials for jumping forward — a course-and-distance winner on good ground — and wears a hood to maintain concentration; his true style is closer to hold-up than front-running, but with pace at a premium he is the likeliest horse to vacate the rear pack and race prominently, which would be a significant upgrade on his mapped position.
runners_data.comment: Ran on into third last time beaten two and a half lengths off this same mark, though drifted across the track on the undulations — landed a handicap at Redcar on the penultimate start off a 5lb lower rating and is effective at 5-6f on a sound surface; the mark looks fair but the wayward tendency is a reservation.

runners_data.name: Power Of Chora
runners_data.note: Ramsden's charge has finished 6th-8th repeatedly on good ground and standard ground, the weakest recent record in the field; wears cheekpieces (tp) to sharpen focus but has not threatened in seven starts, and the tight draw and competitive pace profile here make life harder rather than easier.
runners_data.comment: Below form in first-time cheekpieces over a shorter trip last time, beaten eight lengths — effective at 6f and stays 7f on the all-weather; this trip is easier but the form line makes a confident recommendation difficult despite a lower mark.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Wine
runners_data.note: Second over 5f on soft ground represents the standout form line, but that soft run may flatter given today's good-to-firm conditions; Dods runs both Sparkling Wine and Brain Freeze, splitting trainer stats, and at OR 45 this filly is at the bottom of the handicap with more to find against proven hold-up rivals in a race that will not set up for late closers.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on her handicap debut, beaten four and a quarter lengths from a low weight with the speed in her pedigree to handle 5f on good to soft — able to race off the same mark here and could build on an encouraging first handicap start; yet to win but our rating puts her at the top of this field.

runners_data.name: Tanaka
runners_data.note: O'Meara's runner wears a hood (hg:h) and carries form over 5f on good ground, with Shay Farmer booked; though naturally a hold-up type by design, his speed figures suggest he could push forward if space opens up, though recent form (7th, 5th, 6th in last three) offers limited encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Out of form across recent starts, beaten five lengths most recently — effective at 5f on a sound surface and wears first-time headgear today; looks well held on current evidence and needs to show considerably better than seen recently.

races.paceDynamic: Oasis Cover is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f Beverley sprint and, with no genuine rival to push them off the front, C Horgan should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a lung-busting early blast. Behind the leader, the field is packed with hold-up types — Brain Freeze, Power Of Chora, Sparkling Wine, Tanaka, Jack Rabbit Slims and Dabbling all want to come from off the pace — meaning Oasis Cover faces no early pressure and can conserve energy through the first two furlongs before kicking for home on the rising Beverley finish. The closers will be racing in a compressed group with no natural split between them, forcing several to chase from the same position with no tactical advantage over one another. The field holds more hold-up types than the track and distance can realistically accommodate in their natural position — Brain Freeze and Tanaka, both with proven early pace and win form at this trip on good ground, are the most likely to push forward and secure a prominent berth rather than settle tamely at the rear. The dominant tactical verdict is clear: Oasis Cover's uncontested lead on fast ground at Beverley — a track that rewards a prominent, well-judged run — strongly favours the front-running profile, with the one genuine threat coming from any hold-up horse quick enough to track the pace in a forward position from the outset.

scenarios.body: If a second horse challenges Oasis Cover hard for the lead early, burning both out and gifting the race to a held-up runner.

watchPoints.text: Oasis Cover's early stride rate is critical — if C Horgan settles too conservatively and invites Brain Freeze or Tanaka to close on the bridle, the uncontested advantage evaporates before the final furlong.

Brain Freeze's hood and prior 5f win on good ground make him the standout danger if Rhys Elliott pushes forward early rather than accepting the rear — watch the first 50 yards to see whether he tracks the pace or sits deep.

Tanaka and Brain Freeze are both trained to be hold-up horses but both have the raw speed for 5f on fast ground — if both push forward simultaneously they could create an unplanned pace battle that scrambles the race shape entirely.

Jack Rabbit Slims requires a genuine pace ahead of him to finish with purpose; if the early gallop is as modest as the pace map suggests, Nicholls will face a dilemma about whether to commit early or wait for a gap that may never come.

Good-to-firm going confirmed for this race by the official going report — any horse with a soft-ground form line (Power Of Chora, Sparkling Wine's best run) may find conditions quicker than ideal, worth noting before the off.
